Chapter Dues In addition to national per capita tax detailed in Title I, Article X, Section 1 of the National Bylaws, each collegiate member of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall pay chapter dues of $36 per semester. If dues are not paid or the member has not submitted a payment plan by the due date, then that member will be on suspension with the chapter (See Article VIII, Section 2 of these bylaws for terms of chapter suspension). If deemed necessary by a two-thirds quorum vote, the chapter may allow for a temporary increase or decrease in chapter dues. The chapter TÂ­reasurer shall issue receipts to brothers upon their payment(s). Section 2. Probationary Dues The probationary dues or payment plans for probationary members of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall be due the day of the national exam. If dues or a payment plan are not secured by that time, that member may not take the exam at that time. Should a probationary member utilize a payment plan, the plan must conclude on or before the date of Initiation so said member may acquire his Initiation materials. Section 3. Payment Plans Each member of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall either pay in full by the chapter deadline or use a pre-approved payment plan as detailed by the Treasurer. The Treasurer may implement an alternate payment plan with any individual member of the chapter with a full report to and approval of the Executive Committee. All payments on plans must be completed one week prior to the National Deadline for dues. All requests for consideration for an alternate payment plan must be submitted in typed format to the Treasurer prior to the payment due date. In accordance to the Guide to Money Management, this Fraternity does not front dues. Section 4. Chapter Accounts The Beta Sigma Chapter shall hold checking and savings account, which shall serve as the chapter treasury. Only the Treasurer, the President, the Vice President, if he so desires, and the Faculty Advisor, if he so desires, shall have access to the chapter accounts. Access shall be defined as having their name on the account and access to online banking. When any of these officers or the Faculty Advisor change, the account shall be updated; prior to the second meeting of the academic year, all required officers shall be added to the chapter treasury and all exiting officers removed. Section 5. Money Access The Treasurer, the President, the Vice President, if he so desires, and the Faculty Advisor, if he so desires, shall have the authority to write checks or use bank issued debit cards on behalf of the fraternity. Any officers in possession of the chapter debit card may appoint another member of the chapter to execute a previously approved expenditure. ARTICLE II. Officers Section 1. Qualifications The Beta Sigma chapter shall act in accordance with the qualifications for officers in Title III, Article IV, Section 2 of the National Bylaws. In accordance with Title I, Article I, Section 15 of the National Constitution and Bylaws, any alumni member wishing to hold office, other than as Alumni Relations Officer, must be transferred to collegiate status by a majority vote of the chapter and assume the responsibilities of that status. Section 2. Music Coordinator In addition to those offices denoted in Title III, Article IV of the National Bylaws, the Beta Sigma Chapter has created the office of Music Coordinator. For officer duties, see Article V, Section 10 of these bylaws. Section 4. Order of Succession The order of succession of officers of the Beta Sigma Chapter shall be: the President, the Vice President, the Secretary, the Fraternity Education Officer, the Warden, the Treasurer, the Alumni Relations Officer, the Historian, then the Music Coordinator. If none of these officers are present, then a straw-poll vote shall be taken to appoint a collegiate member in good standing – chosen by a simple majority vote – to assume leadership of the event. This succession shall be called upon for such reasons as to determine who will lead meetings in the President’s absence, etc. ARTICLE III. Officer Duties Section 1. General Regulations Chapter officers will act in accordance with the duties listed in Title III, Article IV of the National Bylaws. Section 2. President In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter President’s and Vice President’s Duties, the President shall hold the final say in matters of rules of order. 	 Section 3. Vice President The Vice President shall perform those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter President’s and Vice President’s Duties. Section 4. Secretary The Secretary shall maintain physical and digital records containing all minutes, agendas, and other paperwork. He shall also email minutes in a clean, professional format to the chapter no later than 48 hours after the meeting for which they were taken. Section 5. Fraternity Education Officer In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Membership Development, the Fraternity Education Officer shall present a timeline of his intentions for that semester’s probationary recruitment process by the second meeting of the academic semester. Section 6. Warden In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter Warden’s Duties, the Warden shall be in charge of enforcing the accountability policies (Article VIII of these bylaws) and shall have his attendance book at every event. He shall also be in charge of the chapter contact list. Section 7. Treasurer In addition to those duties listed in Title III, Article IV, Section 8 of the National Bylaws and The Guide to Money Management, the Treasurer shall keep track of chapter funds, and be able to give an accurate report on the available amount of chapter funds at any given time. The Treasurer shall present a monthly report to the Executive Committee, utilizing bank statements, etc. The Treasurer is also in charge of the chapter PayPal Account. Section 8. Alumni Relations Officer In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter Alumni Relations Officer’s Duties, the Alumni Relations Officer shall receive an updated email address from graduating brothers following the Ceremony for Graduating Brothers. Section 9. Historian In addition to those duties listed in the Guide to Chapter Historian’s Duties, the Historian shall record the events and lineage of the chapter during each semester in detail, using whatever visual aids he deems necessary. If the Historian cannot attend an event, he shall delegate his duties to a suitable replacement. He shall store each semester’s documentation in both physical and digital form, using a system that is easily used and understood by any member of the fraternity. He will also present the collected documents to the chapter periodically. Section 10. Music Coordinator The Beta Sigma Chapter designates that the Music Coordinator shall adhere to those duties listed on page 8 of the Guide to Chapter President’s and Vice President’s Duties. He will also interface with the chapter in planning social and fraternal events involving the chapter choir. Section 11. Faculty Advisor In addition to the duties listed in the Faculty Advisor Manual, the Faculty Advisor shall be encouraged to attend at least one chapter event per semester. ARTICLE IV. Committees Section 1. Executive Committee In addition to the officers listed in Title III, Article IV, Section 14 of the National Constitution and Bylaws, the executive committee for the Beta Sigma Chapter has been defined to include the Fraternity Education Officer and the Warden. The Executive Committee may vote to approve expenditures of up to $50 at a time without a vote by the chapter. A member of the committee must notify the chapter of how much money has been spent and for what purpose in the following chapter meeting. Section 2. Special Committees The Beta Sigma Chapter may form special committees as needed. This includes, but is not limited to, committees for specific events such as the Ridenbaugh Haunted House or Scrubfest. Each committee is expected to meet consistently and give regular progress reports. The Executive Committee is responsible for overseeing these committees. ARTICLE V. Family Lineage Section 1. Purpose  The Beta Sigma Chapter shall use a Big Brother system to assist with probationary members and to establish a family lineage. Big Brothers are responsible for any questions that Little Brothers may have regarding fraternity traditions or customs. The Fraternity Education Officer should answer any questions pertaining to fraternity history. Big Brothers and Little Brothers will be determined at a meeting prior to the Ceremony for Pledging. Section 2. Selection Process  If a collegiate member in good standing wishes to take on the role of Big Brother, he may volunteer himself to do so. The Fraternity Education Officer, while in office, may not volunteer to be a Big Brother. The selection process for Big and Little Brothers shall be referred to policy. ARTICLE VI. Special Events and Observances Section 1. Recital The Beta Sigma Chapter shall hold an annual recital, in accordance with Title III, Article II, Section 6 of the National Bylaws. Section 2. Mills Music Mission The Beta Sigma Chapter shall annually present at least one Mills Music Mission to the community in addition to those required for probationary membership and Province Workshop. Section 3. Sinfonia Cup The Beta Sigma Chapter shall hold a so-named Sinfoni-Cup each academic year for the purposes of friendly competition and brotherly bonding. Section 4. Haunted House In partnership with the Sigma Zeta Chapter of Sigma Alpha Iota, the Beta Sigma Chapter shall, every year that it is held, participate in a haunted house in the Halloween season for the benefit of the Moscow Food Bank. Section 5. Scrubfest	 The Beta Sigma Chapter shall host the Ridenbaugh Scrubfest prior to the Lionel Hampton School of Music Audition Day. Section 6. Chapter Day Observance Weekend As its Chapter Day falls during the summer, the Beta Sigma Chapter shall hold an observance weekend during the first three-day weekend of each spring semester. Section 7. Lionel Hampton Jazz Festival The Beta Sigma Chapter shall volunteer at the Lionel Hampton Jazz Festival every spring semester. The Chapter is encouraged to manage their own site at the festival. ARTICLE VII. Discipline Section 1. Attendance The Chapter Warden shall record excused and unexcused attendance of members. Should a collegiate member accrue two consecutive unexcused absences from mandatory events in a single semester, the Executive Committee shall send an email notice regarding any unexcused absences. This communication is not considered notice for suspension required in Title III, Article IX, Section 1 of the National Bylaws. Should the member be absent from the next mandatory event, and not provide a response deemed satisfactory by the executive committee within a week, he may be considered for suspension in accordance with the process described in Title III, Article IX, Section 1 of the National Bylaws. Reasons for planned absences must be submitted in writing to the official chapter email address (betasigmabulls@gmail.com). Section 2. Chapter Suspension Members of the Beta Sigma Chapter may be placed on suspension by the chapter in accordance with Title III, Article IX of the National Bylaws. Members on chapter suspension are subject to the conditions of suspension listed in Title III, Article IX, Section 5 of the National Bylaws. Members on chapter suspension must attend meetings. Section 3. Expulsion Should a suspended collegiate member accrue three unexcused absences within the duration of his suspension, his absences may be considered grounds for expulsion in accordance with the process described in Title III, Article IX, Section 3 of the National Constitution and Bylaws. Section 4. Suspended Member Review At the last meeting of each month, the Beta Sigma Chapter shall conduct a review of the status of any suspended members, including a discussion of any changes in behavior related to the individual's suspension. The chapter must hold a vote at this time on whether to remove the member from suspended status. At the second to last review of each semester, the chapter must additionally hold a vote on whether to expel any members who have not had their suspended status removed in accordance with the process described in Title III, Article IX, Section 3 of the National Constitution and Bylaws. ARTICLE VIII. Miscellaneous Chapter Procedures Section 1. Chapter Communication The Beta Sigma Chapter designates that any official fraternity-related communication between members and the Executive Committee should be submitted via email to the official chapter email address (betasigmabulls@gmail.com), the chapter mailbox in the Lionel Hampton School of Music, or in person to the Executive Committee. Section 2. Voting Procedures Votes may only be presented during opened chapter meetings, and only when a quorum of at least one more than half the chapter’s collegiate members is present. The chapter shall follow modified Robert’s Rules regarding all voting; as specified below. A motion is presented by a member A second collegiate member may amend the proposed motion The amendment must follow these rules as if it were its own motion The motion must be seconded by another member The Warden shall call for a vote on the motion Members shall vote upon the motion The Warden will use the following rules for determining the outcome of the vote Motions regarding usage of chapter funds must be presented with a specific monetary value. The vote will pass by simple majority. Members may abstain from these votes. Motions regarding expulsion, initiation, elections, and other situations requiring anonymity shall be conducted by secret ballot. These votes may either be blind or written down and tallied by the Warden. Members may not abstain from secret votes. The chapter may decide by 2/3 majority to postpone a vote for no more than two weeks, after which the chapter must vote upon the motion. Section 3. Professional and Break Semesters National-based Professional Semester: A semester of temporary alumni status given to collegiate members who have left to student teach, intern, etc. See Title I, Article I, Section 14 of the National Bylaws for additional details. Beta Sigma-based Break Semester: A semester of break from fraternal obligations given to brothers due to extenuating circumstances, not defined under the national professional semester, that compromise their academic standing and ability to participate in fraternal events. These brothers are not given a temporary alumni status, as they are still on campus. They are exempt from paying chapter dues, as they will not be actively participating in fraternal events, but still have to pay national dues to remain in good standing with the national fraternity. Brothers do not have to attend fraternal events such as choir, meetings, probationary events, and fundraisers, but are encouraged to attend these events if they are able to do so. Brothers shall only be granted one break semester in their time as an active collegiate member. By the beginning of the following semester, the brother shall return as an active member, unless he has graduated at the end of his break semester or has left to student teach, intern, etc. Subsection 1. Requesting Break Semester The brother requesting a break semester must present his case before the Executive Committee, and the committee will discuss and consider the request. The Executive Committee must then present the case to the chapter’s Faculty Advisor. Subsection 2. Chapter Notification After the Executive Committee and the Faculty Advisor grant approval for the break semester, the Executive Committee or the member in question shall inform the chapter of the member’s break semester. Due to the personal nature of break semesters, the chapter shall only be made aware of the details the member in question is comfortable sharing. Section 4. ASUI Liaison The ASUI Liaison shall be appointed in the fall by the chapter and follow those duties listed in Article V, Section 12 of these bylaws. This is not an officer position. The ASUI Liaison shall relay information to and from the chapter regarding ASUI events, attend all mandatory training for student organizations, and remain in partnership with the Treasurer regarding ASUI funding. ARTICLE IX. Amendments and Reviews Section 1. Amendments These bylaws may be amended at any regular business meeting, provided that the proposed amendment was presented in writing prior to the meeting. See Article IX, Section II of these bylaws for the voting procedure. Section 2. Reviews These bylaws shall be reviewed at least once every academic year and following any major changes to the governing documents listed in Article I, Section 2 of these bylaws. These updated bylaws shall be reviewed no later than December following a National Assembly. ARTICLE X. University of Idaho Policies Section 1. Non-Discrimination Policy The University of Idaho has a policy of nondiscrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, or status as a Vietnam era veteran. This policy applies to all programs, services, and facilities, and includes, but is not limited to, applications, admissions, access to programs and services, and employment.
